headline: A developer has offered every household in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania $10,000 if its data center plan is approved, and many residents are unmoved.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an unusual direct-payment tactic with a clear human angle; a relay of a WSJ report.
importance_line: About 4,500 households face a cash-versus-property-value choice, while the rejected zoning decision, the lawsuit and the construction pause mean the offer is not yet a deal.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports, as relayed in a syndicated copy on Yahoo, that developer NorthPoint Development has told households in Hazle Township, Pennsylvania, that each of about 4,500 would receive $10,000 if its data center, part of a 15-building plan on 1,300 acres, wins approval. Many residents say they remain opposed, worried about noise and property values, and township officials rejected the plan on zoning grounds last November, after which NorthPoint sued.
notes: WSJ original not read; the syndicated page is read at Yahoo. The letters began in June; the date of the WSJ report is not stated.
